fast-pool.name: Fast Pool
fast-pool.summary: Runs two pools on two signer keys: the original Fast Pool and Max500, which caps what any one member may stake.
fast-pool.source: Both contracts are named fastpool-… and are presented as Fast Pool's by its operator. The two deployer addresses differ, so this is a recorded statement rather than something the chain says.

xverse.name: Xverse
xverse.summary: The wallet company, running three signer nodes of its own.
xverse.source: All three contracts are deployed by SP8HK160YD5GHXP69VGA0TC7AQJ1X4CDW3XVERSE, one address, on chain.

stx-lab.name: STX Lab
stx-lab.summary: Runs four signer nodes registered as stackslabs, and the Stacks Labs pool.
stx-lab.source: Recorded by hand, and the two halves do not share a deployer: the four stackslabs contracts are deployed by SP1Q1CZV7X4N1MCW5G96FR3B1MT8XGFB0YTZWAX85 and stacks-labs by SP3RX8RME63CY63G5WZ8XQWZNTYNETYJESQKE071E. That they are one entity is a statement, not something the chain says. slotwatch.dev names three of the stackslabs keys L2-Labs-1 to L2-Labs-3.

members.note: This key also carries SP3DHX7ZHNTCE1WQHJH0T0HY9NNSVT4SWTY2FRCCT.hiro, which is somebody else's contract — so the contract is named here rather than the key.
A different deployer from the four above; grouped here on a recorded statement.

stacking-dao.name: Stacking DAO
stacking-dao.summary: Runs Native Pool itself and delegates the rest of its STX to nodes other people run, one invite-only contract each.
stacking-dao.source: Every contract listed is deployed by SP4SZE494VC2YC5JYG7AYFQ44F5Q4PYV7DVMDPBG, the address behind Native Pool, on chain. The nodes those contracts sit on are run by other operators, which is why this is a stake group rather than an operator one.

members.note: Stacking DAO's own node, not a delegation.
On a key Xverse also signs its own pools with.

same-funder.name: One funder, two nodes
same-funder.summary: Two signer nodes that appeared within a day of each other in August 2026 and now carry a third of the vote between them. Nobody has said who runs them.
same-funder.source: Neither deployer had done anything before: SP1N8F8BBBC60XF6HJBNJHKPRGJ7WZBRGNDJX4YDR was funded with 5 STX on 3 August 2026 and SP30A7BPA23W9G3GR090ZRVE5AAJ2TCXH412ABYJH with 10 STX on 4 August, both from SPCMYWF0F05XA5KRW22875KAD0H7B9WHJJV3N7WC, and both deployed a plain signer-manager and registered it the same day. That is thinner evidence than any other group here, and it is the reason the group has no name: the same address also funded SPZACCJ8XPZ14P7K7NGFMT1BWQYF2JA9DFA2ZR8A, which deployed Assymetric Labs' contract and is not counted here, so it may simply be a custodian paying deployment fees for whoever asks. What makes the pair worth writing down anyway is where their stake came from — see the note on each contract — and that between them they hold more than a third of the vote under no name at all.

members.note: Its members' STX arrived between 10 and 11 August 2026 from addresses that stacked with STX Lab's stackslabs keys through pox-4 — 12.5m STX from SMSH16RHC888ZM0V0CJ8A8PT8512TT17D66MW806, which held 25m with L2-Labs-3 in cycle 139, and smaller amounts from three more.

The same pattern: 20m STX on 10 August 2026 out of SMYMGWMJRBJVVPM3RXB14C8B04C46J65A7Z52E45, which held 20m with L2-Labs-2 in cycle 139, and 10m out of SM1MREN94TZVDYPTZWX9CHA1RF3SM8YGKH6P0X2Q0. Where a staker moves is the staker's decision, not proof of who runs the node.
